item.title: Victorian Portraits: Capturing the Reading Culture of the 19th Century
item.description: These portraits depict Victorian men, women, and children posing thoughtfully with books, reflecting the era's emphasis on literacy and self-improvement. The images capture individuals in formal attire, seated or standing in studio settings, holding diverse volumes from literary works to religious texts. They symbolize education, refinement, and intellectual curiosity during a time when reading was both a social status marker and a means of personal growth. The photographs preserve the fashion and scholarly ideals of the 1800s, offering an intimate look at how Victorians engaged with literature. By showcasing these sitters in their formalwear and bookish poses, the portraits highlight the cultural significance of reading as a symbol of enlightenment and social mobility. The collection provides a visual archive of Victorian aesthetics and intellectual pursuits, blending historical context with artistic craftsmanship to celebrate the era's literary legacy.

item.title: Urban Adoption of 5G Fixed Wireless Access Surpasses Rural Areas
item.description: A new Ookla report reveals that 5G fixed wireless access (FWA), initially designed to bridge the digital divide in rural areas, is now gaining significant traction among urban residents. In Q2 2026, 70% of FWA speed tests originated from city dwellers, compared to 30% from rural regions. While traditional fiber and cable internet still offer faster speeds, FWA's appeal lies in its cost-effectiveness, ease of installation, and flexibility. T-Mobile leads with median speeds of 222.7Mbps, outpacing AT&T’s Internet Air (161.4Mbps) and Verizon’s 5G Home (83.9Mbps). However, these speeds still lag behind fiber-optic (up to 500Mbps) and high-end cable plans (300-1Gbps). Urban users are drawn to FWA for its flat-rate pricing models, which avoid hidden fees associated with traditional broadband services. Additionally, FWA eliminates the need for lengthy installation times, making it a convenient alternative for densely populated areas. The report highlights how 5G FWA is reshaping internet acce

item.title: China's Moonshot AI Negotiates Revenue-Sharing Deals With Microsoft, Amazon, and Google
item.description: China's Moonshot AI is engaged in negotiations with major U.S. cloud companies including Microsoft, Amazon, and Alphabet's Google to establish revenue-sharing agreements for hosting its K3 model. This potential deal could mark the first significant revenue-sharing pact between a Chinese AI firm and a U.S. cloud provider. The discussions highlight the growing influence of China's AI models, which are often more cost-effective than Western alternatives, despite ongoing national security concerns in the U.S. that have led to restrictions on AI chip exports to China. Moonshot is seeking up to 30% revenue from K3-related services on Azure, AWS, and Google Cloud, aligning with terms outlined for major customers using the open-weight model. item.description: Stud or Dud, a new platform by PeopleFinders.com, enables users to perform background checks on potential dates using public records. The service aggregates data such as financial history, property ownership, employment records, and criminal backgrounds into AI-generated reports. While intended to help daters make informed decisions about relationships, the tool raises concerns about privacy, accuracy, and potential misuse. Critics argue that the platform could be exploited by stalkers or lead to false information impacting individuals' lives. item.title: Nvidia's Strong Earnings Drive Market Gains
item.description: Nvidia's recent quarterly earnings report has significantly impacted stock market trends, with futures showing positive movement. The company reported higher-than-expected revenue and profit margins, driven by strong demand for its graphics processing units (GPUs) in data centers and gaming sectors. Analysts highlight Nvidia's strategic investments in artificial intelligence and cloud computing as key factors behind the earnings surge. Market observers note that the tech giant's performance has bolstered investor confidence, particularly in semiconductor stocks. However, experts caution that sustained growth will depend on continued innovation and global demand for AI technologies. The stock market reaction reflects broader optimism about the technology sector's potential, with traders adjusting portfolios to capitalize on Nvidia's success. item.title: Partial Lunar Eclipse and Blood Moon Event on August 27, 2026
item.description: A partial lunar eclipse will occur on August 27, 2026, with Earth's shadow obscuring approximately 93% of the moon's surface. The event will be visible primarily in the Americas, with peak times varying by location: New York at 12:14 am, Chicago at 11:14 pm, and so on. Europe will experience the eclipse during dawn, though viewing conditions may be challenging due to low lunar altitude. The reddish hue of the moon, known as a 'blood moon,' results from sunlight passing through Earth's atmosphere, scattering blue wavelengths and leaving red light to reach the moon. Observers can enhance their view by finding dark locations away from light pollution, using binoculars or telescopes, and attending public viewing events. The eclipse will last about three hours and 18 minutes, with the darkest phase reaching a magnitude of 0.93. This innovation addresses challenges with unstable or toxic proteins that are traditionally difficult to manufacture. Researchers led by Professor Dan Mulvhill demonstrated that VNp increases protein yields while making production more accessible for researchers and pharmaceutical companies. item.title: Carl Van Vechten's 1934 Photos of Salvador Dalí and Man Ray Amid Surrealist Tensions
item.description: In 1934, American photographer and writer Carl Van Vechten captured iconic images of Salvador Dalí and Man Ray during their time in Paris. The photographs, taken against a backdrop of commercial posters advertising products like toothpaste and cheese, reflect Van Vechten's fascination with avant-garde cultural figures. Despite his late start in photography, Van Vechten was deeply connected to the Surrealist movement, though both artists had complex ties to it. Dalí, who had recently faced temporary excommunication for suspected fascist sympathies, and Man Ray, who never officially joined the Surrealists, posed for the American artist in an optimistic setting. The images highlight their artistic personas during a period of political and cultural upheaval. Both artists would later flee France, underscoring the turbulent era they navigated. Van Vechten's work provides a rare glimpse into the lives of these influential figures at a pivotal moment in art history.

item.title: Major calving event at Petermann Glacier reduces ice tongue by 22%
item.description: A massive ice island, roughly the size of Manhattan Island, has broken away from Greenland's Petermann Glacier after years of growing fractures weakened its floating ice tongue. This event, documented by an international research team led by the University of Ottawa, marks the largest Arctic calving since 2020 and the glacier's biggest loss of floating ice since 2012. The newly separated iceberg, measuring 76.4 km², is approximately 150 meters thick and provides scientists with a rare opportunity to study how large Arctic ice masses interact with ocean currents. Satellite data from the European Space Agency revealed deteriorating conditions along the glacier's central ice tongue, leading to its detachment on August 4, 2026. Researchers predict two additional sections will break off, reducing the ice tongue by 22% and potentially impacting shipping routes. item.description: The article examines how right-wing activists and conspiracy theorists have spread false claims that transgender women compete in the Women’s National Basketball Association (WNBA). It highlights figures like Sydney Watson, who falsely assert that trans athletes are infiltrating the league, and Sophie Cunningham, a WNBA player accused of promoting misinformation. The piece details how these narratives often lack factual basis, with the WNBA explicitly stating there are no transgender players in its ranks. It also explores the broader societal impact of such conspiracies, including the stigmatization of LGBTQ+ athletes and the erosion of public trust in sports institutions. The article underscores the importance of fact-checking and critical media literacy in combating misinformation. Additionally, it critiques the political motivations behind these claims, linking them to far-right agendas that seek to undermine gender equality and diversity initiatives. item.title: Amazon Acquires DuckLabs to Integrate DuckDB Team into AWS
item.description: Amazon has agreed to acquire DuckLabs, bringing its team behind the popular open-source DuckDB database into AWS. The deal aligns with Amazon's strategy to transform S3, its cloud storage service, into a platform for data analysis rather than mere storage. The acquisition includes co-founders Hannes Muhleisen and Mark Raasveldt, who will continue leading the DuckDB project from Amsterdam. DuckDB remains free and open-source under the MIT license, overseen by the DuckDB Foundation. Analysts note that Amazon's move reflects a pattern of acquiring successful open-source projects to monetize them through cloud services. Jordan Tigani of MotherDuck suggests this could strengthen DuckDB's adoption, as Amazon has an incentive to keep it open and widely used to drive compute usage on its infrastructure. item.title: Ohio GOP Governor Candidate Defends Domestic Abuse Accused Rep Amid Midterm Elections
item.description: Ohio Republican gubernatorial candidate Vivek Ramaswamy defended Rep. Max Miller, who faces allegations of domestic abuse against his ex-wife and daughter. A leaked audio recording shows Ramaswamy justifying his support for Miller, emphasizing the importance of preserving GOP control in key midterm races. The accusations against Miller include pouring hot water on his ex-wife, holding a gun to her head, and leaving their 2-year-old daughter with a broken collarbone. Miller has denied all claims and refused to drop out of the race despite calls from GOP leaders like Sen. Bernie Moreno. Ramaswamy, a former Trump advisor, argued that compromising GOP control in Congress would be disastrous. The controversy highlights tensions within the Republican Party as midterm elections approach, with critics calling for Miller's resignation while others defend his right to remain in the race.

The ad, funded by the National Republican Senatorial Committee, framed the April 2026 semi-truck accident near Columbus, Ohio, as a consequence of lax immigration policies. Husted's campaign claimed the naturalized citizen involved in the crash used multiple names and dates of birth to obtain identification, but the Soposki family disputes this narrative. Jesse Mallen, Lynnea's brother, condemned the ad as exploitative, stating, 'Our grief is not raw material for a campaign.' The family's photo was also used without consent, with the copyright held by a friend. item.description: Bobby Charles, the Republican nominee for Maine governor, revealed in an audio recording obtained by The Associated Press that he plans to request federal agents, including Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) officers and U.S. Marshals, to be stationed at polling locations during the upcoming midterm elections. The proposal, which critics have labeled as 'deeply alarming' and 'likely illegal,' involves asking White House border czar Tom Homan to deploy these agents weeks before Election Day. Charles claimed his intent was to ensure election officials could communicate with federal authorities to prevent violence, intimidation, and illegality at polling sites. However, the Department of Homeland Security denied any plans to send ICE agents to polling places, emphasizing that elections are for American citizens, not illegal aliens. item.title: Yale study identifies C3 protein as key to mitigating age-related inflammation through calorie restriction
item.description: A groundbreaking study by Yale researchers suggests that targeting the C3 protein could offer a pathway to reduce age-related inflammation without requiring severe calorie restriction. The research, published in Nature Aging, reveals that caloric limitation reduces chronic inflammation (inflammaging) by modulating immunometabolic checkpoints involving fat-derived molecules and immune cells. While extreme calorie reduction has long been linked to extended lifespan in animals, this study identifies a biological mechanism that could enable similar benefits with less dietary restriction. The team discovered that fat tissue produces specific signaling molecules that suppress overactive immune responses driving inflammation. By manipulating these pathways, the researchers observed reduced inflammatory markers in both human cells and animal models. item.title: Democratic strategist outlines key tactics for winning over Trump supporters in rural Iowa
item.description: The video features a senior Democratic strategist analyzing the challenges of mobilizing voters in traditionally Republican counties within Iowa. The expert highlights the importance of targeted messaging that addresses economic concerns, healthcare access, and local infrastructure improvements. They emphasize the need to counter misinformation about social programs while appealing to working-class voters' priorities. The discussion also covers the role of grassroots organizing and the significance of early voting locations in rural areas. The strategist warns that without a clear plan to engage Trump-supporting communities, Democrats risk losing key swing districts. The analysis underscores the complexities of winning over voters who have historically favored Republican candidates, requiring nuanced strategies that balance ideological messaging with practical policy solutions.

Biggs, who previously defended opposing a 2013 bill targeting the FLDS sect's practices, claimed he was aware of the situation but argued the legislation was too broad. Critics, including survivors and advocates, condemned his past inaction, highlighting the prolonged suffering of victims. The bill, which cleared the state House but died in the Senate, aimed to strip local authorities of power over the sect. item.title: Xbox Launches Disc-to-Digital Program for Physical Game Owners
item.description: Microsoft is introducing a new disc-to-digital program that allows Xbox owners to convert physical game discs into digital entitlements. This initiative, announced ahead of testing for Xbox Insiders starting August 31, lets players claim a digital copy of most Xbox One and Series X disc-based games by simply inserting the disc into a console and launching it. Once claimed, the game becomes playable digitally without needing the physical disc, and users can access features like Xbox Play Anywhere and Xbox Cloud Gaming. Microsoft emphasizes that physical discs will continue to function as before, but the digital entitlement is tied to a single account. Key limitations include revokable licenses per game disc, meaning reselling or lending discs could transfer the digital entitlement. Publishers must opt-in for their games to support this feature, explaining why not all titles are included. Older discs from original Xbox and Xbox 360 are excluded due to manufacturing methods. item.title: Dolly Parton's Early Advocacy for Workplace Equality in '9 to 5'
item.description: Dolly Parton's debut film role in *9 to 5* (1980) marked her as a pioneering advocate for workplace equality. The film, starring Jane Fonda and Lily Tomlin, follows three women who retaliate against sexual harassment by their boss, Franklin Hart. Parton's character, Doralee Rhodes, embodies resilience against gender-based mistreatment, delivering a memorable scene where she confronts Hart with a gun, declaring her refusal to tolerate indecent proposals. This moment solidified her status as both a screen star and an activist. Beyond the film, Parton’s advocacy for women’s rights and Black Lives Matter emerged early in her career, contrasting with her initial focus on music. Her role in *9 to 5* highlighted systemic workplace harassment, a pressing issue even in 1980. item.description: SpaceX is advancing its Starbase Louisiana project, which involves constructing over ten new launch pads for the Starship system. This initiative surpasses previous plans for Texas-based facilities and aims to support ambitious goals like launching one million orbital data centers (Starmind) and supporting NASA's Artemis lunar missions. The project, located on Pecan Island in Louisiana, will cover 506 km²—larger than the combined Kennedy Space Center and Cape Canaveral facilities—and will include a Gigabay for assembling Starship rockets, a Starfactory for building satellites, and infrastructure for orbital data centers. item.title: Britain Paid Slaveholders Until 2015 Despite Abolishing Slavery in 1833
item.description: In 1833, the British Parliament passed the Slavery Abolition Act, which ostensibly ended slavery across the British Empire. However, this legislation was a disguised commercial agreement that compensated slaveholders with £20 million (equivalent to over £16.5 billion today) for losing their enslaved workforce. The compensation came from public funds, effectively making taxpayers pay for centuries of exploitation. This debt lingered as government bonds, which were sold and resold over generations, until 2015 when the UK finally settled the last remaining obligation. The article reveals how this system perpetuated inequality, as descendants of enslaved people in the Caribbean and Britain continued to bear the financial burden while former slaveholders' families—like the Gladstones, Blairs, and Camerons—remained wealthy. item.description: A resurfaced 2017 video of Natalie Harp, former executive assistant to President Donald Trump, has intensified scrutiny over her claims of a medical error that allegedly left her with cancer, chronic pain, and financial ruin. item.description: The FBI and Department of Justice have disrupted a Chinese state-sponsored hacking network that used proxy tools to target U.S. government agencies and critical infrastructure. The operation dismantled two tools, QTRouter and QScan, allegedly linked to a group called QTFY, which is tied to Nanjing Xinjiuwei Network Technology Company. Prosecutors claim the company provided access to botnets of hacked IoT devices and commercial proxy services, enabling Chinese state actors to conduct cyberattacks since 2018. Targets included NASA, the Federal Reserve, the U.S. Senate, the Justice Department, and infrastructure sectors like power companies, hospitals, and defense contractors. Experts note the campaign focused on espionage rather than direct sabotage, though it highlighted vulnerabilities in U.S. systems. During an interview ahead of the PGA Tour Championship, Scheffler acknowledged the difficulties of managing travel demands and time away from home while maintaining his role as a devoted parent. He described the experience as a 'balancing act' that requires constant effort, noting that being a husband and father adds significant responsibilities beyond athletic competition. item.description: In an interview conducted by MS NOW's Alex Tabet, Canadian voters in Ontario voiced their discontent with President Donald Trump's aggressive trade policies and recent threats against Canada. item.title: Legal Challenges Emerge Over Trump's USPS Mail-In Voting Plan
item.description: Democratic attorneys general from 23 states have filed an emergency lawsuit to block a new Postal Service rule that would grant the U.S. Postal Service unprecedented control over mail-in voting. The policy, issued by the Trump administration, allows the agency to establish voter lists and withhold ballots from voters deemed ineligible. New York Attorney General Letitia James condemned the move as an 'unacceptable risk' that could create confusion and threaten voting rights. The lawsuit, filed in Massachusetts federal court, follows a previous Supreme Court dismissal of similar claims as premature. A judge has already temporarily blocked the policy from taking effect. Democratic Party groups are also pursuing legal action against the directive, with U.S. District Judge Carl Nichols requesting proposed schedules for hearings. Trump has long criticized mail-in voting, claiming it is riddled with fraud, but his attempts to reshape voting systems have faced legal hurdles.

item.description: The Chicago Bears concluded their final training camp practice at Halas Hall, featuring notable developments across the roster. Starting right tackle Darnell Wright exited early with an injury to his previously injured arm, raising concerns about his availability. Defensive tackle Gervon Dexter Sr. also left with an injury, while tight end Hayden Large and cornerback Dontae Manning were sidelined. However, safety Elijah Hicks and rookie linebacker Keyshaun Elliott returned from the PUP list, as did quarterback Tyson Bagent and cornerbacks Tyrique Stevenson, Jaylon Johnson, Terell Smith, and Jaylon Jones. item.title: Princess Anne's Courageous Stand Against a 1976 Kidnapping Attempt
item.description: On March 20, 1974, Ian Ball, an armed loner, attempted to abduct Princess Anne along The Mall near Buckingham Palace. The incident unfolded when Ball forced their limousine to stop, brandished two pistols, and demanded Princess Anne exit the vehicle. Her calm refusal to comply, coupled with a brief argument to stall him, allowed time for intervention. Four individuals were injured during the confrontation: her bodyguard Inspector James Beaton, chauffeur Alex Callender, journalist Brian McConnell, and constable Michael Hills. A passerby, Ronald Russell, intervened by striking Ball in the head, enabling police to arrest him. Queen Elizabeth II later honored the bravery of those involved, awarding Beaton the George Cross. Ball was sentenced to life imprisonment in a high-security psychiatric hospital. item.title: Raymond Camden Shares LEGO Screensaver for Mac Users
item.description: Raymond Camden, a developer and LEGO enthusiast, created a screensaver that randomly displays LEGO set information. Using Rebrickable's LEGO dataset, he filtered out non-buildable items and developed an OSX screensaver with Cursor. The project faced challenges with macOS caching but was eventually successful. The screensaver shows random LEGO sets with details like year, name, piece count, and images. Users must whitelist the app via terminal to run it. The project highlights the intersection of AI development, LEGO fandom, and macOS customization. Camden's work demonstrates how developers can leverage existing datasets to create engaging, educational tools for tech-savvy users.

item.title: Ross Douthat Officiates Wedding for Tech Billionaire with AI Ambitions
item.description: Ross Douthat, former New York Times columnist and CBS News correspondent, officiated the wedding of Leopold Aschenbrenner, a 24-year-old hedge fund manager whose $45 billion fund collapsed. Douthat connected with Aschenbrenner after reading his 165-page manifesto predicting AI-driven superintelligence. The couple, Leopold and Avital Balwit, hosted Douthat's family during a road trip, sharing AI predictions that astounded children. The wedding in Carmel attracted Anthropic employees, AI philosophers, and investors tied to Aschenbrenner's fund. Despite his fund's 67% monthly loss and regulatory scrutiny, Aschenbrenner's vision of AI unlocking cosmic resources persisted. The Greenhouse Gas Reduction Fund faces contention as Tier 3 programs risk reduced allocations if higher tiers lack sufficient funds. Senate Bills like SB 913 aim to integrate distributed energy resources like home batteries and electric vehicles into the grid, while SB 868 simplifies solar installation for renters. Meanwhile, Trump-era rollbacks of California's environmental authority are prompting countermeasures, including restrictions on offshore drilling and coal exports. Lawmakers also face pressure from utilities threatening consequences if wildfire liability protections aren't enacted. item.title: Hurricane Preparedness: Lessons from Katrina and Essential Survival Tips
item.description: The article details personal experiences and practical advice for surviving natural disasters, focusing on Hurricane Katrina. The author emphasizes the importance of preparedness, including backup power sources, GPS coordinates, emergency communication tools, and water storage. Key takeaways include maintaining a NOAA Weather Radio, keeping portable chargers and spare cables, using zip-top bags to protect electronics, and storing at least one gallon of water per person per day. The author also highlights the value of having emergency cash and duplicating supplies in vehicles. The narrative underscores the need for flexibility and multiple options during crises, as demonstrated by the author's reliance on a helicopter rescue during the disaster. item.description: A growing number of U.S. service members are seeking formal discharge as conscientious objectors, with two organizations reporting the sharpest spike in decades. The Center on Conscience and War (CCW) noted a sixfold increase in applications since Operation Epic Fury began against Iran, with over 140 applicants already processed compared to around 50 annually. item.description: The Alaska Senate race between incumbent Dan Sullivan and Democratic challenger Mary Smith has become a focal point of national political discourse. Sullivan, a Republican known for his pro-business stance and support for energy development, faces an uphill battle against Smith, who has gained traction by emphasizing climate change policies and healthcare reform. Key issues include Alaska's oil industry regulations, Medicaid expansion, and the state's economic recovery post-pandemic. Sullivan's campaign highlights his experience as a former governor and his bipartisan approach to infrastructure projects, while Smith's team frames the race as a choice between 'business-as-usual' and progressive reforms. item.title: SpaceX's $100 Billion Louisiana Spaceport Aims to Boost Launch Capacity and Job Creation
item.description: SpaceX announced plans to invest up to $100 billion in constructing a new Starship launch facility in Vermilion Parish, Louisiana. The project, dubbed 'Starbase, LA,' is positioned as the primary hub for SpaceX's Starship rocket, which represents the company's largest and most advanced reusable spacecraft. The initiative could support thousands of annual launches and aligns with Elon Musk's broader ambitions to expand SpaceX's Starlink satellite network, deploy orbital data centers, and eventually colonize Mars. item.title: Scientists Identify Genetic Mutation Linked to Rise in Drug-Resistant Malaria
item.description: A study led by Brown University researchers has identified a genetic mutation called PIN that is contributing to the rapid spread of drug-resistant malaria in sub-Saharan Africa. The mutation, which affects the px1 gene, was found in 84% of malaria parasite samples from northern Uganda and 55% from eastern Uganda by 2024. This mutation reduces sensitivity to lumefantrine, a key component of the artemether-lumefantrine drug combination. The PIN mutation emerged around 2008 and spread rapidly, outpacing genetic recombination processes. Parasites with this mutation showed stronger resistance to certain antimalarials compared to those without it. While previous research linked Kelch13 (K13) mutations to artemisinin resistance, the PIN mutation provides the first validated marker for lumefantrine resistance. The study highlights urgent needs for improved surveillance systems and new treatments as drug resistance threatens malaria control efforts in Africa and beyond.

item.description: The article examines Treasury Secretary Jack Lew's strategy to economically weaken Iran through sanctions, blockades, and reduced oil exports. It highlights how Iranian oil shipments to China have declined sharply, with Chinese refiners seeking alternative supplies. The piece notes Iran's deteriorating economy, including an 88% annual inflation rate and food price hikes of 128%, which could fuel domestic unrest. However, it argues that economic coercion alone may not compel Iran to surrender, as the regime has historically framed resistance to foreign pressure as a form of political legitimacy. The text also critiques the U.S. approach for sparing major Chinese banks, potentially allowing Iran to persist through sanctions evasion. It raises concerns about the long-term costs of prolonged engagement, including depleted missile interceptors and a shrinking Strategic Petroleum Reserve. The article concludes that without clear victory conditions or strategic clarity, the economic pressure

item.title: AI-Generated Fake Animal Imagery Threatens Real Content and Trust Online
item.description: The article explores how AI-generated fake images of animals are undermining authentic content and causing trust issues online. It highlights cases like Mibbby Butler, who fell victim to a scam using deepfake animal photos, and organizations like We Animals struggling to combat misleading content. Experts warn that AI-produced rescue videos could mislead viewers about wildlife conservation efforts. The piece also discusses technological solutions such as metadata tags and verification tools aimed at distinguishing real from synthetic media. While acknowledging the creative potential of AI art, the article emphasizes the urgent need for transparency and regulation to protect genuine animal welfare advocacy and prevent exploitation of users' trust.

item.title: Trump Reflects on Dolly Parton's Legacy Following Her Passing
item.description: President Donald Trump addressed the public mourning of singer Dolly Parton, who died at 80, by expressing personal admiration for her. During an appearance on the Glenn Beck Show, Trump discussed his decision to order American flags to be lowered to half-staff in honor of Parton, a rare move that sparked questions from Beck about its significance. Trump emphasized that Parton 'really liked me' and described her as someone who transcended political divides, noting she had equal numbers of Republican and Democratic fans throughout her career. He also highlighted the extended mourning period, which lasted until sunset on September 1, longer than the tributes for other public figures. While acknowledging Parton's non-political stance and refusal to take sides, Trump framed his actions as a natural tribute to someone he considered a personal friend. The article underscores the intersection of celebrity culture and political commentary in contemporary American society.

item.title: MAGA Hosts Criticize GOP's Inaction on Midterm Campaign Spending
item.description: Pro-MAGA radio host Jesse Kelly accused Republicans of committing malpractice by hoarding campaign funds ahead of the midterm elections, which are just 10 weeks away. Kelly, citing a conversation with former Trump press secretary Sean Spicer, claimed the GOP is sitting on a 'gargantuan amount of money' and failing to spend it strategically. Federal filings corroborate Spicer's claims, showing MAGA Inc.'s super PAC held nearly $404 million at the end of July but spent nothing on Republican candidates that month. Instead, funds went toward administrative costs like consulting fees and event photography. Texas serves as a case study, where Democratic state Rep. James Talarico outspent Republican Ken Paxton by over 20 times in a deadlocked race. While MAGA Inc. did spend $830,000 on a Senate primary runoff, critics argue the GOP is missing opportunities to influence key battlegrounds. Kelly's concerns reflect broader anxieties about the party's strategy amid shifting political dynamics.

item.title: Judge rejects executive privilege claims in Comey daughter's firing case
item.description: A federal judge rejected the Trump administration's attempt to invoke executive privilege to block the investigation into the firing of Maurene Comey, the daughter of former FBI Director James Comey. U.S. District Judge Jesse Furman denied the government's request, ruling that the case should proceed without pausing for privilege claims. The Justice Department had argued that the case would force a collision between the executive and judicial branches, citing Supreme Court precedents. However, Comey's lawyers contended that the privilege claim was premature and unfounded, noting that previous cases involving executive privilege concerned records directly related to the president or vice president. Furman agreed, stating that the discovery sought by Comey was relatively targeted and could be managed through standard court procedures. Comey alleges she was fired due to her father's political ties to Trump or her own political views, though the government has since conceded she was an 'ou

item.title: Trump's Economic Sanctions Target Iranians, Impacting Students and Remittances
item.description: The article details how the Trump administration's new economic sanctions on Iran are disproportionately affecting ordinary citizens. The National Iranian American Council (NIAC) criticizes the policy for suspending humanitarian exemptions that allowed Iranian Americans to send remittances, universities to enroll students, and sports exchanges. These measures, part of 'Operation Economic Outcast,' aim to sever ties between Iranians and Americans, with experts calling it collective punishment. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent claims the sanctions target Iran's financial networks to isolate the regime. However, NIAC argues this approach is 'dumber' than previous sanctions, as it fails to distinguish between civilians and elites. The policy comes amid an ongoing conflict that has caused significant economic damage. Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesperson condemns the measures as a violation of international law, warning that no sovereign state will accept such bullying. The article highli

item.title: SEC Opposes NFL Players Returning to College Football Amid Eligibility Concerns
item.description: The Southeastern Conference (SEC) has strongly opposed the practice of former NFL players returning to college football, emphasizing that college athletics should remain exclusive to student-athletes. SEC presidents and chancellors argued that allowing NFL veterans to compete again blurs the line between amateur and professional sports, creates unfair competitive advantages, and reduces opportunities for current and future athletes. This stance comes amid growing debates over eligibility rules, with some programs actively recruiting players who have recently left NFL rosters. Coaches like LSU’s Lane Kiffin and Ohio State’s Ryan Day acknowledge the potential benefits of such recruits but face pressure to balance competitiveness with integrity. Critics, including Oregon coach Dan Lanning, argue that once a player enters the NFL, they should not return, highlighting concerns about equity and fairness. The debate reflects broader antitrust issues in college sports, with advocates pushing f

item.title: Alaska Senate Race Features Two Dan Sullivans in General Election Contest
item.description: The Alaska Senate race has taken an unusual turn with the presence of two candidates sharing the same name, Dan Sullivan. The incumbent Republican Senator Dan Sullivan and the challenger Dan J. Sullivan, a retired teacher from Petersburg, both advanced to the November general election. The challenger's candidacy was contested due to allegations of voter confusion, but a state Supreme Court ruling confirmed his eligibility. The race, which uses a ranked choice voting system, adds complexity as third- and fourth-place finishers could influence the outcome. President Donald Trump endorsed the incumbent, labeling the challenger's candidacy as an attempt to mislead voters. Meanwhile, the Senate race is one of several key contests on Alaska's primary ballot, including the state's lone U.S. House seat and governor race. The incumbent and Democratic candidate Mary Peltola are the leading contenders, with significant fundraising and name recognition. The presence of two Sullivans highlights the

item.title: PCE Inflation Report and Nvidia Earnings Outlook for August 26, 2026
item.description: The U.S. Department of Commerce is set to release the Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) inflation report for August 26, 2026, which will provide critical insights into the nation's inflation trends. This report, a key indicator of consumer price changes, will highlight whether inflation is moderating or persisting despite recent Federal Reserve efforts to curb it. Analysts anticipate the PCE data will show a slight deceleration in inflation compared to the previous month, with core PCE (excluding volatile food and energy prices) likely remaining stable. Meanwhile, Nvidia (NVDA) is scheduled to report its quarterly earnings, which will be closely watched for signals about the semiconductor industry's performance. Investors will be particularly interested in revenue growth, guidance for future quarters, and any mentions of AI-driven demand. The earnings call will also provide context on Nvidia's strategic moves in data centers and gaming, which have been pivotal in its recent stock

item.title: Dog Treat Founder Promotes Organic, Nutrient-Dense Products for Pets
item.description: Sarah Goldberger, CEO of Lord Jameson, an organic dog treat company, emphasizes the use of natural ingredients like blueberries and herbs to create healthy snacks for pets. She avoids artificial colors, flavors, and preservatives, ensuring her products are gluten-free and toxin-free. Goldberger founded the brand in 2019 after her late dog, Jameson, faced health issues linked to medication toxicity. Her treats, which have an 18-month shelf life without preservatives, address digestive sensitivities in dogs and cater to specialized dietary needs like colitis or diabetes. The company's vertically integrated operations in Boulder, Colorado, ensure cost stability and North American sourcing. Goldberger also incorporates plant-based medicine into wellness products, reflecting a holistic approach to pet health. Her commitment to transparency and quality has made Lord Jameson popular among pet owners seeking safer, more natural options for their animals.

item.title: South Carolina Senate Race: Ralph Norman's Supporters Boo Trump's Involvement as He Concedes Defeat
item.description: In South Carolina's Republican Senate primary, Ralph Norman, a 73-year-old congressman, lost to Darline Graham in a contentious race. Norman's supporters booed President Donald Trump's role in the contest during his concession speech, highlighting growing frustration with Trump's political interventions. Graham secured 52.5% of the vote compared to Norman's 47.6%, according to the Associated Press. Trump celebrated his endorsement on Truth Social, claiming Graham's victory as a testament to his influence. Norman, who also lost the GOP gubernatorial primary in June, expressed disbelief at Trump's involvement, stating, 'I never understood why he got in this race.' He criticized the $8 million in PAC spending against him, contrasting it with his reliance on South Carolina donors. Norman's remarks, including a sarcastic comment about the state, drew mixed reactions from his crowd. The incident underscores tensions within the Republican Party, with grassroots activists questioning Trump's g

item.title: Jack White Honors Dolly Parton with Emotional Performance of 'Jolene' at London Show
item.description: Jack White paid heartfelt homage to late icon Dolly Parton by performing a powerful rendition of her classic song 'Jolene' during his concert at the Eventim Apollo in London. The performance, which marked the first time he had played the track since 2007, came shortly after news of Parton's death at age 80. White's cover of the 1973 hit, previously featured on The White Stripes' 2000 B-side 'Hello Operator,' resonated deeply with fans and critics alike. The tribute extended beyond music, as White shared a black-and-white photo of Parton on Instagram, calling him 'Instant Sainthood.' His label, Third Man Records, also released a joint tribute highlighting Parton's legacy as an artist and philanthropist, noting her work through initiatives like the Imagination Library. Tributes poured in from global stars including Elton John, Taylor Swift, and Miley Cyrus (Parton's goddaughter), while Glastonbury organizer Emily Eavis recalled her 2014 performance at the festival. item.title: Treasury's bond-buying strategy faces scrutiny from former mentor
item.description: The article explores the escalating conflict between Scott Bessent, U.S. Treasury Secretary, and his former mentor Stanley Druckenmiller over Treasury's expanded long-dated bond-buying program. Druckenmiller, using an AI-assisted essay, criticizes Bessent's approach as 'price management' rather than liquidity management, arguing it risks distorting market signals. The piece draws parallels to a Shakespearean tale where a mentor undermines his protege's policies. Druckenmiller highlights the tension between Treasury's asymmetric information about markets and the Federal Reserve's market-purist stance. He warns that artificially suppressing long-term yields could delay necessary fiscal reforms, while Bessent defends the program as a tool for improving liquidity. The debate reflects broader concerns about U.S. fiscal sustainability, with private investors like hedge funds now playing a dominant role in Treasury markets—a shift from the foreign reserve-buyer dynamics of the 2000s. item.description: The article discusses the latest developments in the stock market, with a focus on Nvidia and Xpeng as key players shaping current investment strategies. Analysts highlight Nvidia's advancements in AI chip technology and Xpeng's progress in autonomous vehicle development as critical factors driving investor interest. The piece explores how these companies are navigating competitive landscapes, with Nvidia facing challenges from emerging rivals while Xpeng aims to solidify its position in the electric vehicle sector. item.description: The article examines the recent public reemergence of Melania Trump, the former first lady, and her husband's Pentagon advisor, Jennifer Hegseth, highlighting controversies surrounding their roles. item.title: Dolly Parton's Legacy Honored with Global Tributes and Pink-Lit Empire State Building
item.description: The iconic singer-songwriter, Dolly Parton, has passed away at the age of 74, prompting an outpouring of tributes from across the globe. Her death was announced by her family, marking the end of a remarkable career that spanned over seven decades. Parton's legacy includes not only her Grammy-winning music but also her significant contributions to philanthropy, including the Imagination Library and support for vaccine research. In honor of her life and work, the Empire State Building in New York City will be illuminated with pink sparkly lights at 9:25 p.m., a tribute to her iconic song '9 to 5.' Additionally, the mayor of Sevier County, Tennessee, where she was born, declared August 26 as a day of mourning. President Trump ordered flags at the White House to be lowered to half-staff, while prominent figures like Barack Obama, Beyoncé, and Paul McCartney shared heartfelt messages. Her impact extended beyond music, with her advocacy for LGBTQ+ rights and support for various charitable ca

item.title: Iran and Oman Propose Temporary Shipping Lane in Strait of Hormuz Amid US Sanctions
item.description: The article details the geopolitical tensions surrounding the Strait of Hormuz, where Iran and Oman have proposed a temporary shipping lane to address maritime security concerns. This plan aims to establish a demining effort and facilitate safer passage for vessels through the critical waterway. Meanwhile, the United States has intensified its sanctions campaign against Iran, targeting sectors such as aviation, shipping, technology, gold, and digital assets like cryptocurrency. These measures are part of 'Operation Economic Outcast,' designed to sever Iran's economic lifelines. The US Treasury Department is also pressuring countries that maintain economic ties with Iran, threatening secondary sanctions on those that refuse to comply. China has criticized the US actions, warning that they will exacerbate tensions and disrupt global trade. Iranian officials have vowed to counteract the sanctions, emphasizing their preparedness to withstand economic pressure. The proposed shipping lane be

item.title: Dolly Parton's Films Resonate with Queer Communities Through Themes of Acceptance
item.description: The article explores how Dolly Parton's iconic 1980s films became a cultural touchstone for LGBTQ+ communities, emphasizing themes of camp, rebellion, and radical acceptance. Documentary filmmakers Gary and Larry Lane analyze how her film roles solidified her legacy as an enduring LGBTQ+ icon, highlighting the universal appeal of her work beyond traditional narratives. The piece underscores how her characters embodied resilience and authenticity, fostering connections with queer audiences who found representation in her storytelling. It also mentions tributes from celebrities like Andy Cohen and Melissa Etheridge, who praised Parton's advocacy for LGBTQ+ rights. The article notes her quotes about individual freedom and self-acceptance, which continue to inspire contemporary discussions on identity and equality. By examining both her artistic contributions and personal philosophy, the piece positions Parton as a pivotal figure in shaping cultural attitudes toward inclusivity.

item.title: Gang War and Legal Battle Over Tupac Shakur's Murder Trial
item.description: A former Compton gang homicide detective testified during the trial of Duane 'Keffe D' Davis, accused of leading the 1996 murder of rapper Tupac Shakur, that the evidence points to his gang being responsible. The prosecution argues Davis was in a Cadillac that fired fatal shots at Shakur while he was with Death Row Records founder Suge Knight in Las Vegas. Retired Detective Robert Ladd testified that the Mob Pirus gang retaliated against the Southside Crips after Shakur's killing, leading to a violent gang war with 54 other gangs involved. Law enforcement anticipated retaliation and conducted extensive searches, finding links between Davis' associates and the crime scene. However, defense attorney Michael Sanft disputes the evidence, claiming Davis fabricated his presence in Las Vegas and that the detective's testimony lacks concrete proof. The trial highlights the complex interplay of gang rivalries and legal accountability in a high-profile case with lasting cultural impact.

item.title: Canada Imposes Retaliatory Tariffs on U.S. Goods Amid Escalating Trade Dispute
item.description: On August 25, 2026, Canada announced new retaliatory tariffs of up to 50% on hundreds of American goods, escalating tensions in the ongoing trade war with the United States. The measures, set to take effect on September 8, target steel and aluminum imports, which will face doubled tariffs, alongside levies on approximately 700 other products. This action follows the implementation of U.S. tariffs on Canadian goods earlier that week, marking a significant intensification of the bilateral trade conflict. The decision reflects Canada's frustration with the U.S. policies, which it views as economically harmful and protectionist. Analysts note that this development underscores the deepening divide between the two nations, despite their historical alliance. The tariffs are expected to impact industries reliant on imported materials, potentially leading to higher costs for consumers and businesses. item.title: Lindsay Clancy's Trial Examines Mental Health and Criminal Responsibility in Child Murder Case
item.description: The trial of Lindsay Clancy, accused of murdering her three children, has drawn attention to the complex interplay between mental health and criminal accountability. Prosecutors argue that while postpartum mental health challenges are real, the deliberate killing of children cannot be justified by such conditions. Veteran prosecutor Rep. Tommy Pope highlighted the courtroom's unique dynamics, noting that jurors—particularly women who have experienced postpartum struggles—may view Clancy's alleged psychosis with skepticism. Clancy's defense claims she acted under a command hallucination, likening her experience to being a 'puppet' controlled by an external force. Forensic psychiatrist Gregory Saathoff testified that Clancy's auditory hallucinations were unusual, especially since they ceased after the death of her youngest child. item.title: Intuit Shares Drop Amid Revised Growth Outlook
item.description: Intuit, the financial software company behind QuickBooks, experienced a decline in its stock price following revised growth forecasts that signaled a potential slowdown in business expansion. The Wall Street Journal reported that Intuit's earnings call revealed concerns about stagnant revenue growth and challenges in adapting to evolving market demands. Analysts noted that the company's adjusted guidance for fiscal 2024 fell short of expectations, prompting investors to reassess their positions. This shift comes amid broader economic uncertainties, including inflationary pressures and a tightening credit environment. The stock price dipped by approximately 3% in after-hours trading, reflecting market skepticism about Intuit's ability to maintain its growth trajectory. Industry observers highlighted the need for Intuit to innovate in areas like small business tools and AI-driven services to regain investor confidence. While the company remains a leader in accounting software, the slowdo

item.title: Former State Senator Mike Mazzei Wins Oklahoma GOP Governor's Primary
item.description: In the Oklahoma gubernatorial primary runoff on August 25, 2026, former state senator Mike Mazzei secured the Republican nomination by defeating Attorney General Gentner Drummond. This victory, bolstered by President Donald Trump's endorsement, marks a significant moment in the state's political landscape. Mazzei, who narrowly won the GOP nomination, is now positioned as a strong contender in the November general election against incumbent Governor Kevin Stitt. The race highlighted the influence of Trump's support, which failed to decisively impact multiple candidates this year. Drummond, who led in the June 16 primary, faced challenges in maintaining his momentum. The outcome underscores the competitive nature of Oklahoma's political scene and the strategic importance of presidential endorsements in state-level races. Mazzei's win also reflects broader trends in the GOP's efforts to consolidate support ahead of the presidential election. The results signal a shift in the state's polit

item.title: Dolly Parton’s Literacy Initiative Honored by Library of Congress
item.description: The Library of Congress honored Dolly Parton's Imagination Library, a program that has donated over 300 million books to U.S. children under five since 1995. The tribute came after Parton's death at 80 from cancer, with the library posting an image of her reading to children. The initiative, inspired by her father's illiteracy, provides monthly books to families, aiming to foster a love of reading. Over 14% of young children in the U.S. receive books through the program, which has become one of the world's largest childhood literacy efforts. Parton emphasized that her father's lack of education limited his potential, driving her to create the program. The Library noted her contributions, including donating the 100 millionth book in 2018 and hosting story times. This recognition highlights her dual legacy as a music icon and literacy advocate.

item.title: Battleground Republicans Await Trump’s Support Amid Midterm Challenges
item.description: President Donald Trump's decisive victory in South Carolina's Senate GOP runoff for Sen. Darline Graham has sparked debate among Republicans about his focus during critical midterm races. While Graham's win, secured with Trump's backing, highlights the president's enduring influence in conservative states, strategists are urging him to prioritize battlegrounds like Georgia, North Carolina, and Texas where Democratic candidates pose significant threats. The article details how Trump's campaign machinery, including MAGA Inc.'s $400 million war chest, was heavily invested in Graham's race despite her lack of political experience. However, concerns persist that Trump's attention remains fixated on safe Republican seats rather than swing states where his support could sway the congressional balance. item.title: Innovative stencil method enables efficient carbon nanotube patterning for advanced devices
item.description: Researchers from Skoltech, Harbin Institute of Technology, and ITMO University have developed a novel technique to deposit geometric carbon nanotube patterns without material waste. This single-stage process uses laser-cut metal stencils and nitrocellulose membranes to create precise patterns for optical devices and sensors. By pressing the stencil into the membrane at 200 megapascals, pores are clogged to block nanotube deposition in specific areas. The method avoids etching, solvents, and material loss, preserving nanotube quality while enabling reusable templates. The technique allows aerosol chemical vapor deposition through unclogged regions, resulting in high-resolution patterns. Applications include strain sensors with enhanced conductivity and tunable terahertz lenses for wireless communication. The study, published in Light: Advanced Manufacturing, demonstrates scalability and reusability, reducing costs and improving integration of carbon nanotubes into electronics.

item.title: COLORFUL Launches iGame X870E VULCAN W OC Motherboard With Premium Overclocking Features
item.description: COLORFUL has unveiled its flagship iGame X870E VULCAN W OC motherboard, a high-end PC component designed for overclocking enthusiasts. The motherboard features an all-white iridescent finish with rainbow-like reflections, making it visually striking. Underneath the aesthetic upgrade, the board retains its robust performance capabilities, including an 18+2+2-phase 110A DrMOS power delivery system paired with a graphics card-inspired heat pipe and fin cooling system. This ensures stable operation under heavy overclocking scenarios. The motherboard supports DDR5 memory with speeds up to DDR5-8800+ for Ryzen 9000 processors, DDR5-10600+ for Ryzen 8000, and DDR5-8000+ for Ryzen 7000. It includes dedicated overclocking controls such as a Debug display, BIOS switch, BCLK adjustment, and a one-click overclocking button for simplified tuning. item.title: Fulham FC Enhances Training Quality with New Signings
item.description: Fulham forward Josh King highlighted the elevated training standards at Craven Cottage following the arrival of new talent, including Gonzalo Garcia from Real Madrid. The Spanish youngster scored on his debut against Chelsea, contributing to the team's improved performance. King emphasized the need for players to step up after losing key scorers like Raul Jimenez and Harry Wilson, crediting both the new signings and manager Alvaro Arbeloa's coaching philosophy. He praised Garcia's integration into the squad and the demanding yet effective training methods under the new boss. The article details how the club's pre-season preparations and recent matches showcase the positive impact of these changes, with King expressing confidence in the team's progress toward implementing a more intense playing style.

item.title: OpenAI Faces Leadership Changes Amid Ongoing Executive Departures
item.description: OpenAI has experienced another executive departure, with Chris Malone, former head of data centers, leaving the company. Malone joined OpenAI in March 2025 after working at Meta and Google, but his tenure was short. The Wall Street Journal reported his exit, noting the significance of his role in overseeing the Stargate Project, a $500 million U.S. data center initiative. OpenAI cited reorganization as the reason for Malone's departure, restructuring its infrastructure team under Vice President Sachin Katti. This incident adds to a wave of over 13 executive departures in 2026, including the loss of key figures like Fidji Simo and Denise Dresser. The exodus raises concerns about OpenAI's stability ahead of its postponed IPO, with critics questioning its valuation and profitability. Other teams, such as ethics and safety, have also faced leadership changes, further intensifying scrutiny on the company's management and strategic direction.

item.title: Resilience in Displacement: Ukrainian Seniors Reclaim Joy Amid Crisis
item.description: In the aftermath of war, a group of Ukrainian seniors navigates displacement with unexpected vitality. Through vibrant portraits and creative expressions, they challenge societal expectations of aging and resilience. The project highlights how humor, irony, and playfulness become coping mechanisms in the face of trauma. Artists like Maryna Syrovatka document their stories, revealing that joy and defiance are possible even amid crisis. Participants, such as Nadia who transforms stones into defiant art, embody a paradoxical blend of fragility and strength. The work underscores how displacement can disrupt traditional narratives of aging, offering a nuanced perspective on survival and reinvention. By embracing color, absurdity, and handmade elements, the project reframes displacement not as an end but as a reimagining of life's possibilities.

item.title: Man Arrested for Transporting Guillotine Near Supreme Court

The incident occurred on August 25, 2026, when officers noticed the vehicle around 3 p.m. Tuesday. Le was illegally parked alongside the U.S. Supreme Court building, prompting the police to seize the guillotine and make the arrest. The weapon, a device historically associated with execution, was reportedly parked in a manner that raised security concerns. Authorities emphasized that the arrest was part of their efforts to maintain public safety and prevent potential threats to the judicial institution. The case highlights the strict protocols surrounding the transportation of dangerous objects near government buildings, particularly those with symbolic and historical significance. item.title: A Glimpse into 1930s Automotive Luxury: The Talbot-Lago T150C 'Lago Spéciale'
item.description: The 1938 Talbot-Lago T150C ‘Lago Spéciale’ stands as a quintessential example of prewar French automotive engineering and design. Built on the sophisticated T150C chassis, this sports car was powered by a refined 4.0-liter straight-six engine, offering both performance and elegance. Its extended wheelbase allowed for more graceful coachwork, with many examples crafted by the renowned Figoni et Falaschi firm. These aerodynamic 'teardrop' designs and sleek cabriolets transformed the T150C into a true work of automotive art, blending advanced engineering with exquisite French styling. The Lago Spéciale remains an enduring symbol of 1930s luxury, reflecting the era's commitment to innovation and craftsmanship. The article highlights its historical significance, noting that these vehicles were not just machines but masterpieces of design, capturing the timeless grace and refined beauty of a rare 1938 model. item.title: U.S. Agriculture Secretary Refuses to Disclose Beef Import Sources, Sparks Public Outrage
item.description: U.S. Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins sparked widespread public backlash after refusing to disclose the countries from which the United States will import beef under President Trump's proposed policy. The controversy arose during a press briefing where Rollins declined to specify which nations are in talks about increasing beef imports, citing lack of knowledge. This response ignited fierce criticism from GOP lawmakers and media figures who accused the administration of secrecy and hypocrisy. Senator Ruben Gallego (D-AZ) questioned why the Secretary of Agriculture would withhold information about the origin of U.S. beef, while journalist Aaron Parnas demanded transparency. item.title: North West Aspires to Regular Job at Starbucks After Music Career
item.description: North West, the 13-year-old daughter of Kim Kardashian and Kanye West, has revealed her career aspirations beyond music. In an interview with Dazed, she expressed interest in working at Starbucks when she turns 14, stating, 'I want to have a regular job.' This comment comes after she dropped her six-track debut EP, 'N0rth4evr,' and a music video for 'Aishite.' While she initially considered becoming a basketball player, she now focuses on her musical path. North West also critiqued her peers' interests, noting, 'Everyone’s in love with boys, vaping and doing all kinds of bad stuff,' contrasting her own desires for blue hair and piercings. The interview highlights North West's evolving identity as she navigates fame and adolescence.

item.title: Daylen Lile's Two-Homer Game Doesn't Offset Nationals' Loss to Rockies

item.title: Critics Highlight Oversights in Trump's Midterm Convention Schedule
item.description: The Republican National Convention's schedule for President Donald Trump's midterm event has faced significant criticism for its glaring oversights. Online critics highlighted scheduling conflicts with NFL games, the absence of foreign policy discussions, and the overall lack of strategic planning. The two-day event in Dallas, Texas, was slated to feature Trump and Vice President JD Vance as headline speakers on consecutive nights, coinciding with the start of the NFL season. item.title: Sen. Darline Graham faces criticism for vague responses on affordability and national security
item.description: U.S. Senator Darline Graham, sister of late Senator Lindsey Graham, faced backlash for her vague answers during a Senate hearing. Jen Psaki highlighted Graham's embarrassment when asked about affordability and national security, noting her lack of preparedness. Psaki criticized Trump's attempt to defend Graham, emphasizing the contrast between her focus on affordability and her brother's foreign policy expertise. Graham's response to a question about legislative action on affordability was met with sarcastic remarks from Psaki, who pointed out her current Senate role. The incident underscores growing scrutiny of Graham's qualifications and her ability to navigate complex policy issues, raising questions about her readiness to represent South Carolina in the Senate.

item.title: Lactose Intolerance as a Social Construct: Racial and Historical Influences
item.description: The article explores how lactose intolerance, once considered a medical defect, was historically framed as a racial condition due to systemic biases. It traces the origins of this narrative back to post-World War II America, where dairy producers sought to eliminate surplus milk by promoting its consumption in schools and globally. When people of color experienced digestive issues after consuming milk, scientists labeled it an 'inborn error of metabolism,' assuming lactose tolerance was the norm. This racialized framing persisted despite evidence that most humans are naturally lactose intolerant, with only certain ethnic groups maintaining lactase persistence. The piece argues this narrative is part of broader nutritional imperialism, where Western diets were imposed on others as superior, pathologizing non-white dietary practices like Asian flush or rice-based diets. It highlights how such scientific biases have reinforced racial hierarchies, with modern examples including racist misu

item.title: Federal Judge Rules Trump Administration Violated Court Order on Mail-In Ballots
item.description: A federal judge ruled that President Donald Trump's administration violated a court order blocking new mail-in ballot restrictions, finding officials made contradictory claims to different courts within weeks. U.S. District Judge Indira Talwani determined the Trump-governed USPS defied her preliminary injunction by secretly finalizing a rule implementing Trump's executive order on mail-in ballots just days earlier. The rule would prohibit delivering mail ballots in states that haven't shared voter roll data with federal authorities, facing lawsuits from 26 states and voting rights groups. While the administration argued the rule wouldn't enforce itself for the 2026 election unless injunctions were lifted, Talwani rejected this claim, noting conflicting statements to the Supreme Court. The judge declined penalties but allowed plaintiffs to amend their case to challenge the finalized rule directly. This adds to ongoing legal battles accusing Trump's team of bypassing judicial orders on v

item.title: Generalist's AI foundation model secures $600M in funding for robotics innovation
item.description: Generalist, a robotics startup founded in 2024 by former Google DeepMind researchers Pete Florence and Andy Zeng, has reached a $3 billion valuation after securing additional capital led by 8VC. The latest funding round totals nearly $200 million, bringing the total Series B funding to $600 million since its June announcement at a $2 billion valuation. The company is developing an AI foundation model that enables robots to learn new tasks from short video demonstrations (3-12 seconds). Generalist's Gen 1.5 model is being tailored for specific use cases through customer feedback, though the startup remains relatively quiet compared to competitors like Physical Intelligence ($11B valuation) and Skild AI ($14B valuation). Investors speculate that robotics could reach a 'ChatGPT moment' where general task performance becomes possible without explicit training, but challenges remain due to limitations in internet data access for robot training. The funding reflects optimism about the sector

item.title: Dolly Parton's Enduring Legacy: Kindness, Artistry, and Global Impact
item.description: Dolly Parton, a cultural icon whose influence transcended boundaries, left an indelible mark on the world through her artistry, generosity, and unapologetic authenticity. In a divided society, she became a unifying figure, admired by all demographics. Her success stemmed from embracing her unique identity while radiating radical kindness, making everyone feel included. Beyond her iconic songs like 'Jolene' and 'I Will Always Love You,' Parton built an empire on her own terms, from music to entertainment ventures. Her philanthropy, including the Imagination Library—which mailed over 200 million free books to children globally—and disaster relief efforts, showcased her commitment to giving back. Dollywood, her theme park in Tennessee, became a symbol of her entrepreneurial spirit, generating $1.8 billion annually and creating thousands of jobs. Parton's legacy lies in her ability to blend high camp with deep sincerity, proving that genuine warmth is the most powerful force. Her passing m

item.title: Los Angeles City Council Moves to Regulate Unregulated Phenibut Drug
item.description: The Los Angeles City Council has voted to regulate phenibut, a Soviet-era drug marketed as a 'brain booster' or 'smart drug,' which is widely available in convenience stores across the city. Councilmember Heather Hutt authored the motion, citing concerns about its unregulated sale to minors and the risks of addiction, seizures, hallucinations, and even coma. The proposed regulations include restricting sales to individuals under 21, banning sales near schools and daycare centers, and creating warning labels. Phenibut, which functions similarly to Valium or Xanax by depressing the central nervous system, is not federally regulated and cannot be legally sold as a dietary supplement. Despite its availability in gas stations and convenience stores, Hutt emphasized that the drug's risks are significant, particularly for teenagers who may purchase it without age restrictions. The motion now requires approval from the full council before becoming law. This action follows previous efforts to r

item.title: Trump Biographer Explores Dynamics Between President and Son-in-Law
item.description: A Trump biographer and author of 'Inside Trump's Head' has provided insight into the complex relationship between President Donald Trump and his son-in-law Jared Kushner. Michael Wolff, the biographer, explained that Trump is 'slightly intimidated' by Kushner due to his Harvard education, strategic interactions, and ability to refocus conversations on topics Trump prefers. This dynamic comes amid speculation about Kushner's recent meeting with Rep. Hakeem Jeffries (D-NY), the House minority leader, which Wolff framed as a power play ahead of the 2026 midterms. Kushner, who operates his own independent office, is believed to be preparing for potential Democratic control of the House. Wolff noted that Trump's tendency to defer to family members means he likely did not confront Kushner over the meeting. The discussion highlights broader themes of political maneuvering, familial influence, and the challenges of navigating power dynamics within the Trump administration.

item.title: Dolly Parton Passes Away at 80 After Battle with Cancer
item.description: Country music legend, philanthropist, and global icon Dolly Parton passed away at the age of 80 on August 25, 2026, following a brief battle with cancer. Her death occurred peacefully at the Vanderbilt-Ingram Cancer Center in Nashville, Tennessee, surrounded by loved ones. The article highlights her remarkable career spanning over seven decades, during which she wrote more than 3,000 songs, sold over 100 million records, and earned 11 Grammy Awards. Parton's legacy includes transforming global philanthropy through child literacy programs and medical funding. Tributes poured in from fans, world leaders, and music legends, including Sir Paul McCartney and Jane Fonda. President Donald Trump ordered the American flag to be lowered to half-staff for a week to honor her memory. The piece also reflects on her journey from a Tennessee songwriter to an international icon, emphasizing her iconic aesthetic, self-deprecating humor, and enduring impact on music and culture.

item.title: Trump's Light Schedule Raises Questions About Leadership During Presidency
item.description: The article critiques President Donald Trump's official daily schedule, which was described as unusually light, raising concerns about who is actually governing the country. Political analyst Bennito L. Kelty, writing for Raw Story, highlights that Trump's schedule during a recent Tuesday included minimal substantive events, with most activities occurring during a period labeled 'executive time.' This term, coined during Trump's first term, is said to signify time spent watching TV, posting online, and engaging with sycophantic advisors. The schedule featured a 12:30 p.m. policy meeting, a prerecorded interview at 2 p.m., a closed-press meeting at 3 p.m., and a signing event at 4 p.m., with no intelligence briefings or public engagements. Analyst David Pakman argues that this pattern mirrors Trump's first term, where 60% of his working hours were logged as 'executive time.' Pakman criticizes the schedule as evidence of Trump's diminished stamina and leadership capacity, challenging the

item.title: Secret Service Agents Investigated Over Leaks Linked to Trump's Secret Evacuation
item.description: Three U.S. Secret Service officials were placed on administrative leave and lost their security clearances amid an investigation into potential misconduct related to leaks of classified information. The probe involves allegations that the agents disclosed sensitive details about President Donald Trump's secret evacuation from Turkey in 2026, which was prompted by intelligence about a surface-to-air missile threat to Air Force One from Iran. Journalist Susan Crabtree reported that the FBI and CIA are involved in the investigation, with one of the suspended officials identified as Anthony Guglielmi, the agency's communications chief. The Secret Service spokesperson stated the case is being reviewed by the Office of Professional Responsibility, though no further details were provided. This follows previous incidents where Trump administration officials faced scrutiny for leaking classified information, including a DOJ subpoena targeting New York Times journalists who reported on security

item.title: U.S.-Canada Trade Dispute Threatens Winemaker Industries
item.description: The escalating trade tensions between the United States and Canada are poised to inflict significant economic strain on the winemaking sector, particularly in regions reliant on cross-border trade. Recent negotiations have failed to resolve disputes over tariffs and regulatory standards, prompting concerns about potential retaliatory measures. Winemakers in both countries face heightened risks of increased costs, reduced export opportunities, and disrupted supply chains. The conflict, rooted in longstanding disagreements over agricultural subsidies and trade barriers, has intensified amid broader geopolitical shifts. Industry experts warn that without a resolution, the sector could experience a decline in production and profitability, affecting both small-scale producers and large vineyards. The situation also raises questions about the long-term viability of trade agreements and their impact on local economies. Stakeholders are urging policymakers to prioritize dialogue to mitigate th

item.title: Jesse Watters Acknowledges Abdul El-Sayed as a Competent Opponent in Senate Race
item.description: In a notable development, Fox News anchor Jesse Watters publicly acknowledged Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed as a worthy opponent during a segment of 'The Five.' The exchange followed a heated debate where El-Sayed, a physician and political figure, challenged Watters on various cultural and policy issues. Watters admitted to initially doubting El-Sayed but ultimately expressed grudging respect, stating, 'I like him.' The discussion included contentious topics such as gender-affirming care for children, with El-Sayed countering Watters' questions by pointing out the circumcision of males as a common surgical alteration. Additionally, El-Sayed subtly undermined Watters' Republican opponent, Mike Rogers, by implying he was uncooperative. This segment highlights shifting dynamics in political discourse, where even adversarial figures can acknowledge each other's strengths, reflecting broader tensions in U.S. politics.

item.title: Instagram Introduces New Editing Tool to Streamline Reels Creation
item.description: Instagram has launched a new editing feature called 'First Draft' to simplify the process of creating Reels. This tool automatically trims video clips, removes pauses, and compiles the best moments into an initial cut, which can be completed in under 10 seconds. The feature is designed to save creators time and make video editing more accessible for those without advanced editing experience. While similar tools exist in other platforms like Adobe Firefly and CapCut, Instagram's integration of this functionality directly into its app reduces the need for users to switch to external editors. The feature is initially available on iPhones and can be accessed during video recording or from the Reels gallery. Additionally, Instagram is developing other tools, such as an AI assistant for video editing and a feature to group related Reels into series. The announcement coincided with Instagram head Adam Mosseri's anticipated testimony in a high-profile social media addiction trial against Meta.

item.title: Jeanne Lafaurie: A Pioneer of Mid-Century Parisian Fashion
item.description: This article celebrates Jeanne Lafaurie, a visionary French couturière whose work in mid-20th-century Paris redefined elegance and sophistication. As a master designer, Lafaurie collaborated with iconic figures like André Courrèges, blending avant-garde techniques with timeless aesthetics. Her creations, characterized by clean lines, luxurious fabrics, and innovative silhouettes, became synonymous with the era's fashion revolution. The piece highlights her influence on haute couture, her role in shaping Parisian style during a transformative period, and her enduring legacy through iconic garments and photographs. From the 1940s to the 1960s, Lafaurie’s work captured the essence of post-war elegance, blending artistry with practicality. Her contributions extended beyond fashion, as she mentored emerging designers and championed sustainable practices long before they became mainstream. The article also explores her personal life, including her relationships with contemporaries like Yves

item.title: Data Centers Fuel Rapid Expansion of Gas-Powered Energy Infrastructure in the U.S.
item.description: New research reveals that the amount of gas-fired power projects developed specifically for data centers in the U.S. has nearly doubled in under a year, reaching over 189 gigawatts as of mid-2026. This surge highlights the growing reliance of tech companies on private fossil fuel plants to power data centers, driven by the rapid expansion of artificial intelligence's energy demands. Global Energy Monitor tracked this increase, noting that gas projects for data centers jumped from 4 gigawatts in early 2024 to 97 gigawatts by late 2025. The shift to behind-the-meter plants allows data center builders to bypass grid connection delays and avoid higher utility costs for ratepayers. However, this trend raises significant climate concerns, as inefficient turbines in many facilities could lead to emissions surpassing those of small to medium-sized countries. The U.S. now leads China in gas plant development for data centers, contrasting with China's focus on renewables like solar and hydropowe

item.title: Supreme Court Justice Clarence Thomas Faces Impeachment Allegations Over Podcast Comments and Gifts
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Clarence Thomas has drawn criticism for comments made during an appearance on Senator Ted Cruz's podcast, where he praised Republican allies for defending him and his wife against allegations related to their efforts to overturn the 2020 election. Legal expert Glenn Kirschner warned that Thomas's remarks, which included thanking GOP senators like Mike Lee for standing by him during attacks, undermine any claim of impartiality. Kirschner argued that the comments provide a clear basis for congressional impeachment inquiries, as they reveal potential partisan bias and conflicts of interest. The legal analyst also connected Thomas's remarks to undisclosed gifts from GOP donors, including a $250,000 motorcoach, home renovations for his mother, and private-school tuition for his great-nephew. Kirschner outlined a prosecutor's roadmap for impeachment, emphasizing the need to subpoena financial records and follow evidence of potential misconduct. The article highlights gr

item.title: Dolly Parton's Sister Criticizes Trump's Leadership and Behavior Before Her Death
